newsitem.title: UK: Hoare Govett nudges up FTSE 100 year-end target.
newsitem.headline: Hoare Govett nudges up FTSE 100 year-end target.

text.p: Strategists at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett raised their year-end forecast for the FTSE 100 index as part of a broad review of forecasts prompted by an increasingly negative view on the mark, market sources said on Wednesday.

The brokerage's still-cautious view on the FTSE is that it will end the year at 4,000, up slightly from its previous 3,900 forecast but still well below the index's current near-record level above the 4,300 point.
The FTSE was up 9.7 points at 4,342.0 by 1445 GMT.

Sources said Hoare Govett had cut its 1997 forecast for the mark to $1.75 from $1.60, arguing that only further weakness in the German currency will lift growth and allow Germany to meet Maastrict debt criteria.
Expectations of low continued mark weakness -- and consequent relative sterling strength -- were enough to trim half a percentage point off Hoare Govett's forecast for UK GDP growth this year.

The brokerage also cut half a point off its UK inflation forecast and a quarter point off its year-end UK interest rate forecast to 6-1/2 percent, sources said, sligthly improving the appeal of equities here.
Strategists at the brokerage declined comment.
